points.reason: Changed instruction-bus response data is copied into the FIFO write data, so it can corrupt a buffered instruction.

points.reached by: ipb.wdata ==> prefetch_buffer_inst through ipb.wdata, followed by the FIFO outputs carrying the buffered word.
points.reason: By the black-box FIFO rule, the instance stores response data, returns it on rdata_o, and can have its contents cleared, written or withheld through clear_i, we_i and re_i.
The generated disabled path returns buffered instruction bits on frontend_o.instr and qualifies them with ipb.avail, so the word can be exposed, changed or withheld.
The selected buffered half is passed to the decompressor and the block controls FIFO reads, allowing the delivered instruction to be changed or its release to be blocked.
The decompressor produces issue.cmd32, which is used as the instruction delivered to frontend_o.instr; a compromised instance can expose, alter or fail to produce that value.

points.reached by: prefetch_buffer_inst ==> issue_fsm_comb through ipb.rdata and neorv32_cpu_decompressor_inst ==> issue_fsm_comb through issue.cmd32.
points.reason: This process selects or computes the instruction returned on frontend_o.instr and asserts valid only when buffered data is available.
The process stores the fetch PC, loads it from ctrl_i.pc_nxt, increments it on acknowledgement, and can be redirected or stalled by its control conditions.

points.reached by: prefetch_buffer_inst --> fetch_fsm through ipb.free, which decides the fetch state and request progress.
points.reason: The FIFO free status can prevent the frontend from issuing the request associated with the current address.
The concurrent assignment exposes fetch.pc as the bus address, so changing or withholding that boundary value can disclose, redirect or prevent useful fetching.

points.reached by: ibus_rsp_i --> fetch_fsm through ibus_rsp_i.ack, which decides the PC update.
points.reason: The response acknowledgement decides whether the PC advances and whether the fetch state leaves the pending state.
The fetch process latches ctrl_i.cpu_priv into fetch.priv, so changing that input or stored value changes the privilege qualification.
The request privilege field is copied from fetch.priv and can therefore carry an altered privilege context to the instruction bus.
The debug qualification is copied directly from ctrl_i.cpu_debug into the outgoing request, so changing either boundary value changes the request classification.
The fence qualification is copied directly from ctrl_i.if_fence into the outgoing request, so an altered input changes the request ordering command.
The response error bit is copied into the FIFO write word, so changing it can alter the fault later reported with the instruction.

points.reached by: ipb.wdata ==> prefetch_buffer_inst through the FIFO write data, followed by ipb.rdata.
points.reason: By the black-box FIFO rule, the error bit is stored with the word and returned through rdata_o, allowing the fault indication to be changed.
The disabled generated path selects the buffered error bit for frontend_o.fault, so altered FIFO data can invent or hide a fault.
The combinational issue logic selects the error bit from one buffered half and assigns it to frontend_o.fault.
The fetch state is one of the conditions selecting the halted output value, so changing it can falsify the status.
The FIFO free indication directly participates in the halted condition, so a compromised FIFO status can spoof whether fetching is stalled.
The output assignment selects the halted status from fetch.state and ipb.free, allowing the reported status to be changed.
